blocks.title: When the rear tire slips
blocks.content:
A rider reaches a loose patch on a climb and stands to keep the same speed they would hold on pavement. The next pedal stroke spins the rear tire. They shift weight, push harder, and lose more momentum.

On a climb like this, ease the pedal force and choose a gear you can turn smoothly. If the grade or surface still makes that impossible, walking is a useful way through. The goal is to keep making progress while you have control.

blocks.label: Pedal pressure you can repeat
blocks.content: On a familiar, mild gravel climb, use a gear that lets you turn the pedals without a sudden shove at the top of each stroke. Stay seated while it feels comfortable and keep enough weight over the rear tire for it to drive. Your hands stay ready to steer, not to pull the bike side to side.

Climbing on loose ground asks you to manage the force reaching the rear tire. A sudden surge can make the tire spin, especially when the surface changes under you. Shift to an easier gear before the steepest part if you can see it coming. Keep your effort steady and let speed change with the hill.

Standing can be useful when you need to move or change position. It also changes how weight and pedal force reach the bike. On a loose section, try a controlled seated effort first. If the tire slips, ease the stroke, shift when the chain is under less load, and find a firmer line. Do not grind a hard gear to meet a cadence target.

blocks.title: Climb with traction in mind
blocks.description: Use a familiar climb with a clear route and an easy way to stop or walk.

steps.detail: Find the firmer visible line. Check where the grade or ground changes.
Select a gear that lets you pedal smoothly before you have to push hard. Ease pedal pressure while shifting.
Stay seated while comfortable, steer gently, and let your pace slow if the hill demands it.
Ease the next pedal stroke and look for a firmer line. If control does not return, stop safely and walk the section.

blocks.content: During a race, a loose climb starts after several hours of riding. Shift early and accept a slower pace through the worst patch. A brief walk may cost less time than repeated wheelspin and a stalled restart. Decide from the surface and how you feel, not from a target power number.

### Check your gearing on the bike

Before an event, find a familiar climb similar to the hardest grade you expect. Use the gear you would still want late in the ride. If you have to shove the pedals to keep them moving, make a note of the gear and surface. Consider an easier gear before the event rather than discovering the limit on the course.

blocks.title: Smooth climb repeats
blocks.description: Use a short, mild gravel climb. Compare the feel of two comfortable gears without chasing a fixed cadence or making the tire slip on purpose.

variants.label: Familiar mild climb
steps: Check the climb for traffic, loose patches, and a place to stop. Start at an easy effort.
Shift to an easier gear before the steeper part and pedal with an even stroke.
On a second pass, use a different comfortable gear. Notice whether one lets you steer and pedal with less strain.
If the rear tire slips, ease the effort and choose a firmer line. Stop or walk if you cannot regain control.

variants.label: Surface change on a familiar climb
steps: Choose a climb where you can see a firmer section followed by a modest loose patch.
Shift while still on the firmer ground. Keep your hands ready to steer and reduce pedal force if the tire starts to slip.
After the climb, note the gear, line, surface, and whether you would change the approach next time.

proof_gate.description: You can choose a gear before the loose section and respond calmly if the rear tire slips.
proof_gate.target: Complete a familiar mild climb with a controlled stroke, or stop and walk when traction is uncertain.

blocks.title: If you stall on a climb
steps: Stop where you can put a foot down safely. Keep clear of riders or traffic behind you.
If the slope is too loose for a controlled restart, walk to firmer ground.
Restart in an easy gear after you have a clear line. Do not force a mount on a steep or crowded section.

blocks.question: You reach a loose patch on a familiar climb and the rear tire spins. What is the next useful move?

options.text: Stand and push harder to regain speed
Ease pedal force, find a firmer line, and stop or walk if control does not return
Keep the same power and spin the tire until it grips

blocks.explanation: A smoother stroke and a firmer line may restore traction. Walking is appropriate when the section cannot be climbed under control.

blocks.content: On your next easy gravel climb, write down the gear you chose before the loose section, the line you used, and what happened when you changed pedal pressure.
The next lesson covers reading the surface before it reaches the wheels. You can use that early information to choose a line, gear, and pace.
